question: Which of the following best defines impulse in mechanics?

options.text: The product of mass and velocity
The product of force and the time for which it acts
The rate of change of momentum multiplied by the distance
The change in displacement over time

solution:
The correct answer is __**The product of force and the time for which it acts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Impulse** in mechanics refers to the **product of force and the time interval** over which the force acts. This is a correct statement.
 
• Mathematically, impulse (J) can be expressed as **J = F × Δt**, where F is the force applied, and Δt is the time duration for which the force acts.
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity, which means it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• The unit of impulse in the SI system is **Newton-second (Ns)**.
 
• Impulse is directly related to the change in momentum of an object, as per **Newton's second law of motion**: **J = Δp**, where Δp is the change in momentum.
 
• The concept of impulse is crucial in understanding collisions, as it explains how force and time contribute to the changes in the momentum of objects during impacts.
